calls.prompt:
Draw one new anatomical exercise illustration: the CONVENTIONAL BARBELL DEADLIFT, start position (bar on the floor, athlete set up and gripping it).

IMAGE 1 is the canonical athlete. Copy him exactly: the same bald, faceless, muscular anatomical male; white and light-grey skin, crisp muscle separation, fine dark-grey contour lines, soft grey shading; smooth featureless pelvis with no genital detail, no shorts, no underwear, no clothing of any kind; the same plain white trainers. Same proportions, head, hands, feet, limb thickness and line weight. Polished flat 2D anatomical illustration.

IMAGE 2 is the trap-bar deadlift from the same library. Copy its CAMERA and its drawing of the grey plates and steel sleeves: the athlete is seen from the FRONT THREE-QUARTER, facing the viewer and turned about 30 degrees to the picture's right, camera at hip height. Do not copy its hexagonal trap bar or its handles.

IMAGE 3 is the same deadlift drawn from behind. Use it ONLY for the pose and the equipment: one straight Olympic barbell with ONE grey bumper plate on each end, the bar resting on the floor at mid-shin height, the grip just outside the shins. Do not copy its rear camera.

SCENE: pure black background. Nothing under the athlete: no floor line, no platform, no shadow, no reflection. No text, labels, arrows, numbers or logos. Exactly one person. The whole athlete, both plates and both bar ends are inside the picture with black space around them.

CAMERA: front three-quarter, as in IMAGE 2. We see the athlete's face side, chest, the front of both thighs and shins, and the near side of his hips. The barbell runs across the picture in front of his shins, slightly diagonal because of the three-quarter turn; the near plate is a little larger than the far plate.

POSE (start): feet hip-width apart and flat, toes slightly out, the bar over the middle of the feet and touching the shins. Hips hinged back and set ABOVE the knees, shoulders slightly in front of the bar, back flat and neutral from hips to head, chest up, neck neutral with the head looking a little ahead on the floor. BOTH ARMS ARE STRAIGHT and hang vertically, hands gripping the bar overhand just outside the shins. Knees bent and pushed slightly out over the toes.

MUSCLE COLOURS: the glutes and the hamstrings are filled solid medium violet #7B72E9 where they are visible. The spinal erectors and the trapezius are filled a lighter lilac #9590E0 where they are visible. Every other muscle stays white-grey. The colour never changes muscle size or hides the contour lines.

Square picture, the athlete large in the frame.
